definition: A marsupial is a mammal belonging to the distinct order Marsupialia. In the source, marsupials are mentioned as one of several separate mammalian orders and include the carnivorous Thylacinus.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Mimicry; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not define “marsupial” as “a mammal belonging to the distinct order Marsupialia,” nor does it state that marsupials are a taxonomic order.
The packet mentions “carnivorous marsupial Thylacinus” only as an example within a discussion of biological resemblance (mimicry/convergence), not as a definition of the term “marsupial.”
The definition’s taxonomic framing (order/affiliation) and the claim about marsupials as one of several separate mammalian orders are not supported by the provided text.
The packet does not define “marsupial” as such; it only mentions “Marsupialia” as one of three mammalian orders in an example about convergent resemblance.
The statement that marsupials are “a mammal belonging to the distinct order Marsupialia” is an unsupported dictionary-style definition rather than something established in the supplied source.
The claim about Thylacinus is supported only as an example of a carnivorous marsupial; the packet does not support the broader definitional wording in the first sentence.
